sentences.en: We get support from UC Davis, a globally ranked university working to solve the world's most pressing problems in food, energy, health, education, and the environment.
sentences.zh: 我们得到了加州大学戴维斯分校的支持，这是一所全球排名前列的大学，致力于解决世界在食品、能源、健康、教育和环境方面最紧迫的问题。

sentences.en: UC Davis researchers collaborate and innovate in California and around the globe to find transformational solutions.
sentences.zh: 加州大学戴维斯分校的研究人员在加州乃至全球范围内开展合作与创新，以寻找变革性的解决方案。

sentences.en: It's all part of the university's mission to promote quality of life for all living things.
sentences.zh: 这一切都是该大学促进所有生物生活质量这一使命的一部分。

sentences.en: Find out more at 21stCentury.ucDavis.edu.
sentences.zh: 欲了解更多信息，请访问 21stCentury.ucDavis.edu。

sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: Saluto.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: Let me start with this.
sentences.zh: 让我从这一点开始说起。

sentences.en: The invented language of Esperanto has a flag, and it kicks ass.
sentences.zh: 人造语言世界语有一面旗帜，而且它酷毙了。

sentences.en: Green field, white canton in the upper left corner with a green five-pointed star on it.
sentences.zh: 绿色的底面，左上角有一个白色方块，上面有一颗绿色的五角星。

sentences.en: I'd be on board because of the design of the flag alone.
sentences.zh: 光凭这面旗帜的设计，我就愿意支持它。

sentences.en: Seriously, I could march in the streets behind that flag, but that's not the Esperanto way at all.
sentences.zh: 说真的，我愿意举着这面旗帜走上街头，但这根本不是世界语的风格。

sentences.en: Esperanto is about hope.
sentences.zh: 世界语代表着希望。

sentences.en: It was created in the 1880s by a Polish eye doctor named Ludwig Zamenhof,
sentences.zh: 它是由一位名叫路德维希·柴门霍夫的波兰眼科医生在19世纪80年代创造的，

sentences.en: and he lived in this town, Bialystok, where there were Poles, Jews, Germans, and Russians,
sentences.zh: 他住在比亚韦斯托克这个小镇，那里住着波兰人、犹太人、德国人和俄罗斯人，

sentences.en: and they all spoke different languages, and they all hated each other.
sentences.zh: 他们都说着不同的语言，而且彼此仇视。

sentences.en: So he had this idea that if everybody spoke a common language, they could communicate,
sentences.zh: 于是他产生了一个想法：如果每个人都说一种共同的语言，他们就能交流，

sentences.en: they could get to know each other as people, and there wouldn't be any more racism or conflict,
sentences.zh: 他们就能作为人去了解彼此，也就不会再有种族主义或冲突了，

sentences.en: which is a beautiful idea.
sentences.zh: 这是一个美好的想法。

sentences.en: This is Sam Green.
sentences.zh: 这位是萨姆·格林。

sentences.en: My name is Sam Green.
sentences.zh: 我叫萨姆·格林。

sentences.en: I'm the director of Utopia in Four Movements.
sentences.zh: 我是《乌托邦的四个乐章》的导演。

sentences.en: One of the four movements of Sam Green's live documentary is about Zamenhof's Utopia of Esperanto.
sentences.zh: 萨姆·格林这部现场纪录片的四个乐章之一，讲的就是柴门霍夫的世界语乌托邦。

sentences.en: In some ways, the history of Esperanto really mirrors the 20th century in a certain flowering of utopian energy
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，世界语的历史确实反映了20世纪乌托邦能量的某种繁荣，

sentences.en: and ultimate waning of that by the end of the century.
sentences.zh: 以及到世纪末这种能量的最终衰落。

sentences.en: Zamenhof's full dream of peace through a shared second language never came to pass.
sentences.zh: 柴门霍夫通过共享第二语言来实现和平的完整梦想从未实现。

sentences.en: According to estimates, somewhere between 50,000 and 2 million people speak Esperanto.
sentences.zh: 据估计，全世界大约有5万到200万人会说世界语。

sentences.en: But that shouldn't suggest that Esperanto is a failure.
sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着世界语是失败的。

sentences.en: In the history of invented languages, it's the greatest success story ever.
sentences.zh: 在人造语言史上，它是最伟大的成功故事。

sentences.en: Guest number two, Erika Okrent.
sentences.zh: 第二位嘉宾，埃里卡·奥克伦特。

sentences.en: My name is Erika Okrent, and I'm the author of In the Land of Invented Languages.
sentences.zh: 我叫埃里卡·奥克伦特，是《人造语言之地》一书的作者。

sentences.en: Esperanto was a real product of the time.
sentences.zh: 世界语是那个时代的产物。

sentences.en: In the end of the 19th century, early 20th century, when nationalism was tearing Europe apart,
sentences.zh: 在19世纪末、20世纪初，当民族主义将欧洲撕裂时，

sentences.en: all these old empires were crumbling, and the lines around which they fractured were linguistic ones.
sentences.zh: 所有这些古老的帝国都在瓦解，而它们分裂的界线正是语言界线。

sentences.en: So it made a lot of sense to say, hey, let's find a linguistic solution to our probleMs.
sentences.zh: 所以说“嘿，让我们为我们的问题找一个语言解决方案”是非常合理的。

sentences.en: But the mantle of Esperanto as the king of invented languages also had to do with its design as a language.
sentences.zh: 但世界语作为人造语言之王的地位，也与其语言设计有关。

sentences.en: Well, Esperanto was designed to have as simple as possible a grammar, all nouns and in O, all adjectives and in A.
sentences.zh: 世界语的语法设计得尽可能简单，所有名词以O结尾，所有形容词以A结尾。

sentences.en: Verb tense is indicated by regular endings, and it never varies, so there are no irregular verbs.
sentences.zh: 动词时态通过规则词尾来表示，且从不变化，所以没有不规则动词。

sentences.en: So you learn a finite number of endings and a few root words, and you're up and running.
sentences.zh: 因此，你只需要学习有限数量的词尾和几个词根，就可以上手了。

sentences.en: After a few weeks of learning Esperanto, you can start communicating meaningfully with other speakers.
sentences.zh: 学习世界语几周后，你就可以开始与其他使用者进行有意义的交流了。

sentences.en: But its other strength is that it's not too engineered.
sentences.zh: 但它的另一个优势是它没有过度设计。

sentences.en: Being over-designed is a pitfall of many other invented languages.
sentences.zh: 过度设计是许多其他人造语言的陷阱。

sentences.en: Previous projects tried to be so consistent and regular and break down the entire world of concepts into their component pieces.
sentences.zh: 以前的项目试图做到如此一致和规则，并将整个概念世界分解成它们的组成部分。

sentences.en: Each letter would contain a part of meaning within it.
sentences.zh: 每个字母都包含其中的一部分含义。

sentences.en: Those kind of languages are impossible to use.
sentences.zh: 那种语言是不可能使用的。

sentences.en: Esperanto has this nice, sloppy middle ground.
sentences.zh: 世界语有一种很好的、随性的中间地带。

sentences.en: It's a nice balance between systematicity and arbitrary sloppiness.
sentences.zh: 它是系统性和随意性之间的一种很好的平衡。

sentences.en: And when it comes to language, we need both of those things.
sentences.zh: 当谈到语言时，我们需要这两者。

sentences.en: In our natural languages, we need a way to get more specific when we need to, so we have stuff like legal jargon.
sentences.zh: 在我们的自然语言中，我们需要一种在需要时变得更具体的方法，所以我们有法律术语之类的东西。

sentences.en: But it also lets us just sort of talk without necessarily knowing where we're going with it or knowing exactly what we mean.
sentences.zh: 但它也让我们能够随口交谈，而不必非得知道我们要说什么，或者确切地知道我们的意思。

sentences.en: So for all you language inventors out there, don't make it too perfect.
sentences.zh: 所以对于你们这些语言发明者，别把它做得太完美了。

sentences.en: A little fuzziness is key.
sentences.zh: 一点模糊性是关键。

sentences.en: So is artistic expression.
sentences.zh: 艺术表达也是如此。

sentences.en: From the beginning, Zamenhof stressed poetry and music in Esperanto.
sentences.zh: 从一开始，柴门霍夫就强调世界语中的诗歌和音乐。

sentences.en: And there are unique aspects to the language that make it especially suited to a kind of poetic wordplay.
sentences.zh: 这种语言有一些独特的方面，使它特别适合某种诗意的文字游戏。

sentences.en: With endings, you can make any word into a verb.
sentences.zh: 通过词尾，你可以把任何词变成动词。

sentences.en: So if you have blua, meaning blue, you can also have a verb.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你有blua，意思是蓝色，你也可以有一个动词。

sentences.en: Bluas is bluing.
sentences.zh: Bluas就是“正在变蓝”。

sentences.en: So an Esperantist can say, la cielo estas blua.
sentences.zh: 所以一个世界语者可以说：la cielo estas blua。

sentences.en: The sky is blue.
sentences.zh: 天空是蓝色的。

sentences.en: But if he really wants to be an Esperantist about it, he'll say, la cielo blua.
sentences.zh: 但如果他真的想表现得像个世界语者，他会说：la cielo bluas。

sentences.en: The sky is bluing.
sentences.zh: 天空正在变蓝。

sentences.en: And that's a very Esperanto way of expressing it.
sentences.zh: 这是一种非常世界语式的表达方式。

sentences.en: Any word can also be an adverb.
sentences.zh: 任何词也可以是副词。

sentences.en: Which is strange.
sentences.zh: 这很奇怪。

sentences.en: Not many languages have this feature.
sentences.zh: 没有多少语言有这个特点。

sentences.en: So you don't say, I go to the beach in the summer.
sentences.zh: 所以你不会说“我在夏天去海滩”。

sentences.en: You will say, summerly, I go to the beach.
sentences.zh: 你会说“夏日地，我去海滩”。

sentences.en: Summerly, I go to the beach.
sentences.zh: “夏日地，我去海滩”。

sentences.en: If you do not approve of that sentence, I don't want to live in your dark and joyless little world.
sentences.zh: 如果你不赞同这个句子，我可不想生活在你那黑暗而毫无乐趣的小世界里。

sentences.en: One of the ultimate ironies of Esperanto is that one of its most widespread uses in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 世界语最大的讽刺之一是，它在美国最广泛的用途之一，

sentences.en: was during the Cold War.
sentences.zh: 是在冷战时期。

sentences.en: The U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国，

sentences.en: would do these war games against a fictitious enemy.
sentences.zh: 会针对一个虚构的敌人进行这些战争游戏。

sentences.en: The maneuver enemy, also known as the aggressor.
sentences.zh: 演习中的敌人，也被称为“侵略者”。

sentences.en: And they'd have to have the enemy speaking a different language.
sentences.zh: 他们必须让敌人说一种不同的语言。

sentences.en: And since they didn't want to offend any other country, they couldn't have him speaking Spanish or French.
sentences.zh: 由于他们不想冒犯任何其他国家，他们不能让敌人说西班牙语或法语。

sentences.en: Russian even, they had them speaking Esperanto.
sentences.zh: 甚至是俄语，他们让敌人说世界语。

sentences.en: Esperanto was used by the U.S.
sentences.zh: 世界语被美国陆军使用，

sentences.en: Army, so it wouldn't possibly offend another country and cause some unnecessary conflict.
sentences.zh: 这样它就不会冒犯其他国家并引起不必要的冲突。

sentences.en: So even in this distinctly American, completely twisted context, Esperanto achieved exactly what it was designed to do.
sentences.zh: 所以即使在这种典型的美国式、完全扭曲的背景下，世界语也实现了它被设计出来的目的。

sentences.en: 99% Invisible was produced by me, Roman Mars, with support from Lunar, making a difference with creativity.
sentences.zh: 《99%隐形》由我罗曼·马尔斯制作，并得到了Lunar的支持，他们用创造力创造了改变。

sentences.en: It's a project of KALW, the American Institute of Architects San Francisco, and the Center for Architecture and Design.
sentences.zh: 它是KALW、美国建筑师协会旧金山分会以及建筑与设计中心的一个项目。

sentences.en: To find out more and see the flag of Esperanto, which you really should do, go to 99percentinvisible.org.
sentences.zh: 想了解更多信息并查看世界语的旗帜（你真的应该看看），请访问 99percentinvisible.org。
